one_liner: Calorie tracking app that reads your meal from a photo
audience: 16-30s gym-goers, bulkers and weight-loss beginners who follow fitness creators on TikTok and want macros without manual logging (inferred)
core_pain: manually searching, weighing and guessing every meal's calories and macros in a database, so tracking gets abandoned within a week
old_way_objects: notes app screenshots of nutrition labels
scenes: standing at the kitchen counter at 11pm with a late-night snack, phone in one hand, scrolling a food database for the right entry
at a restaurant with friends, plate arrives, someone is trying to guess the macros of a mixed curry that has no label
in the gym car park after a session, realising they haven't logged anything since breakfast and giving up on the day
proof_points: About 80% accurate on food scans (stated in FAQ)
Photo scan uses the phone's depth sensor to calculate food volume
Tracks calories, protein, carbs and fat; photo scan, barcode scan or describe your meal
Integrates with Apple Health and Google Fit for steps and exercise
Add your own foods and recipes
User quotes: 'im ngl I've lost 17 lbs with it', 'IVE BEEN BULKING FOR A YEAR STRAIGHT W APP'
do_not_say: 100% accurate or perfectly accurate scanning (site says about 80%)
any medical claim: treats, cures or manages diabetes, eating disorders or any condition
guaranteed weight loss or 'lose X lbs in X days'
naming MyFitnessPal as a rival to attack (site only mentions it re: imports)
free forever or no cost (it is a paid subscription after a 3-day trial)
invented user counts, download numbers or accuracy percentages
'you can eat anything and still get shredded' as a brand promise
implying subscriptions transfer between iPhone and Android
cta: Download Cal AI and claim the 3-day free trial
